Area.evidence_source: While inpatient stays in a hospital can have therapeutic benefits, episodes of inpatient care characterized by a loss of dignity can have negative consequences. Preserving dignity can be problematic within health care settings particularly for men in crisis and admitted to a hospital without their consent. Separation from personal belongings (e.g., clothing) and the use of restraints results in losses of dignity and feelings of imprisonment. While inpatients, men often have little to do, are isolated from the other patients, and receive little psychotherapy while on the ward. As a result, many questioned the therapeutic value of their inpatient experience and actively tried to avoid future admissions. To avoid another admission, some of the participants said that they lied about their mental health status when in emergency departments. Others noted that they delayed seeking help even when in crisis.
